angleStats.notes:
RESULT: 0 qualified candidates for Angle 1 (explicit asks, English). I did not open any original post from a Gujarat or Indian builder or broker asking for a CRM, chatbot or WhatsApp automation, or complaining about missed enquiries or telecallers. I returned 0 rather than pad the list.

WHAT THIS TELLS US ABOUT THE PROMPT AND TOOLING (the point of the test):
1. The prompt needs a research model that can read social posts. Google, Bing and DuckDuckGo return vendor SEO pages for these phrases, so explicit-ask posts (LinkedIn, X, Facebook groups, reddit, YouTube comments) were not findable here. Gemini Deep Research has deeper access to Google's index, so a Gemini failure here says nothing about the prompt. This run only shows that Claude's WebSearch and WebFetch cannot test Angle 1.
2. Every query phrased as a pain or an ask ('missing enquiries', 'need CRM', 'WhatsApp automation real estate') is swamped by the CRM and WhatsApp vendors selling to the same builders. There are many local Gujarat options: Makanify and BrokerDost (Ahmedabad), Codingclave (Gandhinagar, from INR 39,999 one-time or INR 3,999 per month), Realatic, Rynow (Rajkot), VSCRM (Surat), DaeBuild (Ahmedabad, since 1998). That suggests two things. (a) Small Gujarat builders are being pitched CRMs constantly, so the cold-pitch bar is higher. (b) Our message should not lead with 'CRM'; it should lead with the WhatsApp first reply and site-visit slot.
3. The prompt's own gates (a signal in the last 14 days, in the builder's own words, a verified real owner, a published contact, a website or LinkedIn) are mostly met by non-explicit signals (job ads, Meta ads with a WhatsApp button, new RERA projects), not by explicit asks. This matches the earlier finding that explicit asks are rare. Expect Angle 1 to yield 0 to 2 leads even on a capable tool.
4. The 'last 14 days' window plus date verification cannot be done from search snippets. Most social results carry no visible date, so a run without browsing and login access cannot satisfy it.

SUGGESTIONS:
- Run this angle only in Gemini Deep Research, or by hand in a logged-in browser by a human, and treat the output as leads to re-verify.
- Put the strongest weight on Angle B signals (Meta Ad Library with a WhatsApp CTA, telecaller or CRM-executive job posts on the builder's own pages, new GujRERA registrations plus active ads). These can be checked from official or ad-library pages with a date.
- If any Apify budget is available next time, the best low-cost run is Meta Ad Library, not Google search.
- The Kautilya Group (Ahmedabad) job page is the only builder-side hint I saw. It is undated and not an explicit ask, so it was not counted. Check it under the hiring angle.

ESTIMATED APIFY SPEND: US$0.00 (the single run was refused at start by the account limit).
TOOL CALLS USED: about 26, mostly WebSearch and WebFetch.

angleStats.notes:
RESULT: 0 candidates for angle 2 (Hindi/Hinglish/Gujarati explicit asks). I took about 33 tool calls (25 was the target). About 8 of those were failed or refused calls, 6 of them for Apify, the DuckDuckGo CAPTCHA, the reddit.com and magicbricks.com domain refusals and an unreadable Facebook page.

WHAT THIS TELLS US ABOUT THE PROMPT (angle 2 only):
1. The exact Hinglish/Gujarati phrases ('enquiry aati hai par reply nahi hota', 'site visit nathi thati', 'builder mate CRM joiye') matched nothing. Not one result contained a first-person post, in any script. Real builders and brokers do not write these sentences in publicly indexable text. Complaints about leads live in private WhatsApp groups or in Facebook group posts a logged-out crawler cannot see. Gujarati-script queries returned nothing relevant, only unrelated pages.
2. Search results for this topic in India are almost entirely CRM, AI-calling and WhatsApp-automation vendors. Without a verified owner identity and a dated post, the output is vendor marketing. Expect Gemini to hallucinate or relabel vendor content here, so every item in an explicit-ask section must be re-checked.
3. This tool cannot do the job the prompt assumes. The search tool ignores the site: operator and cannot read Facebook, Instagram or YouTube post pages or comments. Without Apify (limit hit) there is no route into dated social posts. A research model with a live Google index (Gemini Deep Research) may see Facebook and YouTube text that this tool cannot. So this test does not prove the prompt fails there. It only shows the Hindi/Hinglish/Gujarati explicit-ask signal is very rare and invisible to our tools.
4. Hiring signals did show up, but only as undated job-board snippets (Satyamev Group, TLJ Property, Modak Group, Saanvi Nirman, Samanvay Realty, and the deduped Swagat and NB Developer). They are plausible Tier-2 hiring signals if someone opens the postings and confirms dates. That belongs to the hiring angle, not this one.
5. Suggested prompt changes if Gemini also returns near-zero here: (a) drop or demote the Hinglish/Gujarati phrase list and treat it as a footnote, because behavioural signals (Meta Ad Library with a WhatsApp CTA, dated hiring posts, new RERA registrations) are far likelier to be real; (b) add 'ignore any page from a CRM, AI-calling or WhatsApp vendor' to the search instructions; (c) require the model to quote the post verbatim and give the URL so we can spot-check fast; (d) set the expectation in the prompt that 0 leads in this section is acceptable.
6. Spend: Apify US$0 (refused). No contact, form, account or login was made. Nothing was sent."]

angleStats.notes:
RESULT FOR THE PROMPT, hiring angle: it works as a signal finder but weakly as a lead finder. It produced 1 candidate with a LIKELY owner and 0 VERIFIED, after about 25 tool calls and 13 real-estate employers inspected. The method that worked best was a logged-out LinkedIn public jobs search page fetched with WebFetch and a past-2-weeks filter, followed by opening each job page for date and poster. This gave real dates (relative) in one call per city, which the Weekday and TeamLease aggregators never gave. What limits it:
1. The hiring ads are generic 'sales executive' postings, many apparently templated, with page headers wrongly showing 'Mahesana'. They show growth or staffing, not a visible enquiry-handling pain. No ad said 'telecaller' with enquiry follow-up from a real developer inside the window, apart from the undated Weekday listings.
2. The job poster is often HR, a student or an unnamed person, so the prompt's 'name the real owner and say how verified' rule is the bottleneck. Only Satyamev reached LIKELY, and that rests on one self-asserted LinkedIn label.
3. Dates are relative ('3 days ago'), so each is accurate to about one day, not exact.
4. RERA numbers could only be found on third-party sites, so they are unverified, and the prompt's request for RERA numbers cannot be met without the GujRERA portal.
5. Business-published contacts exist for Satyamev, but WhatsApp capability is unknown.

Ideas to improve the angle: (a) after a hiring hit, add a fixed second step that checks the GujRERA authorised person and the MCA/LLP partners for the owner; (b) combine the hiring signal with a Meta Ad Library check of the same builder's page for a WhatsApp or 'Send message' ad, which would give the stacked signal the brief calls for; (c) try Naukri and Indeed company listings; (d) search Gandhinagar, Anand, Bhavnagar, Mehsana, which were not run; (e) treat hiring alone as Tier 2 context rather than a standalone lead. If you contact Satyamev, the safest route is the company LinkedIn page or the website phone, asking for the MD or sales head by name only after the owner is confirmed. Nothing was contacted, posted or submitted."

angleStats.notes:
RESULT FOR ANGLE 4 (paid-enquiry and launch signals): 0 qualified candidates. Tool calls used: about 23. Apify spend: US$0.00.

HONEST VERDICT ON THIS ANGLE WITH THIS TOOLSET: the prompt's strongest angle-4 signal (Meta ads with a WhatsApp or Send-message button, page name and ad start date) could not be tested at all. The Ad Library is not reachable through WebFetch/WebSearch, and the only Apify route was blocked by the account's monthly hard limit. This is a tooling failure and says nothing about whether such leads exist. Gemini Deep Research with browsing may do better on the Ad Library, but that is unproven. A browser-pane or Chrome session that opens the Ad Library UI manually (read-only, no login) would be the next thing to try.

WHAT WORKED, PARTIALLY: GujRERA registration numbers encode the approval date as DDMMYY (for example MAA17359/160926 is 16 Sep 2026), and gujrera.com project pages show 'RERA approved' and 'last updated' dates. That gives a way to date-check new launches. Sequence numbers around MAA17359 correspond to mid-Sep 2026, so numbers above about 17400 should be Oct 2026 launches. The weak point is discovery: no index page I could reach lists projects by recency, so I only found Auracle (16 Sep 2026) and The Neelkanth Heritage (10 Aug 2026) by luck through search.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR THE PROMPT: the launch route yields promoter names such as LLPs, with no website, no owner and no contact. The 'real owner' and 'website or LinkedIn' mandatory rules would reject almost all of them, which is correct behaviour but means RERA-first discovery is a low-yield, high-effort route for a text-only researcher. Aggregator pages (housing.com, housiey, onlynew) carry 'new launch' tags without dates and must not be trusted as signals.

SUGGESTION: pair the launch route with a human or browser-based Ad Library check for the Auracle project (Ue Living LLP, Makarba) before dropping it. It is the only genuinely new registration found, and whether it runs click-to-WhatsApp ads is unknown.

angleStats.notes:
RESULT: 0 candidates for Angle 5. I am not going to pad this. I opened one thread myself (Oculus Infra), and it fails on date and on pain type. Every other item was seen only as a search snippet and was not opened.

HOW MANY TOOL CALLS: about 24 tools calls in total (both Apify attempts failed immediately). Estimated Apify spend: US$0.00.

WHY THIS ANGLE FAILED WITH THE TOOLS AVAILABLE
1. Buyer complaints with dates sit behind login or bot walls. These are Google reviews (need a Maps scraper, and Apify was over its hard limit), Facebook comments (login wall), MouthShut (403) and Reddit (refused). Open web search surfaces only undated aggregator complaints, and those are about delivery, refunds or maintenance, not 'nobody replied to my enquiry'.
2. The only dated complaint I could verify (Oculus Infra, Ahmedabad) is from Aug to Oct 2025, outside the window. It also complains about post-sale defects, so it is not an enquiry-handling signal.
3. Owner-side posts (launch week, hundreds of enquiries, bad lead response) are almost never indexed by this search tool. The hits were vendor and agency blogs (hyperleap, sell.do, campaignhq, groweon, limechat, opzynic, swiftleads, edesy and similar), which are competitors. Their statistics are marketing claims and must not be reused as facts about any builder.
4. Search results gave no Gujarat builder founder statement dated 21 Sep 2026 or later. I looked for podcasts and interviews. The Speaking Real Estate episodes with Shilp Group and Shivalik Group, and the Ahmedabad Real Estate Review (Bakeri Group) episodes, were not dated inside the window, and nothing in them mentions leads or sales teams.

PROMPT FINDINGS (this is a test of the prompt, so for what it is worth)
- Signal B-5 (public buyer complaints plus builder replying 'call us/DM us') cannot be done with open web search. It needs Google Maps reviews or Facebook page comments pulled by a scraper, plus a list of target builders first. Without Apify it returns nothing. If Gemini Deep Research has Maps and Facebook access this may work there. If the prompt is run from a tool without them, ask the model to say so rather than infer from aggregator pages.
- Founder-side signals (launch week, hundreds of enquiries) are rare and mostly sit in LinkedIn or YouTube. Neither is reachable without logging in or scraping, which our rules forbid. Expect near zero from this angle even in a good week.
- Hazard in the output: this prompt invites the model to treat 'consumer complaint' aggregator pages and agent blogs as evidence. They are undated, anonymous and often a year old. The prompt's date rule is correct and was what rejected the one real thread I found. Keep it.
- Possible useful by-product for other angles: Squareyards listings show Ahmedabad builders with current new launches (Aadi Makers, Tirupati Construction, Kailash Corporation, Sahaj Buildcon, Raghuvir Buildcon, Hrishikesh Ventures, Bhumika Buildcon). These are only names to check against the Meta Ad Library and GujRERA. They are not leads, have no verified owner, and I did not open them.

NEXT STEPS FOR THE OWNER
- Re-run this angle only once Apify has quota (the Google Maps scraper, newest reviews, per builder) with a pre-built builder list from GujRERA or the Meta Ad Library. Then filter reviews posted since 21 Sep 2026 that mention 'reply', 'response', 'call back', 'no one picked up'.
- Treat Angle 5 as a corroboration step on builders already found by the ads, hiring or GujRERA angles, not as a standalone discovery source.

I would regrade it from B to C+ (low B at best). I would send ONE short email to the company-domain address, nothing on WhatsApp, and expect very little. About 19 tool calls used.

SIGNAL REAL AND FRESH (confirmed again): LinkedIn 'Real Estate Salesperson' (Ahmedabad) and 'Sales And Marketing Specialist' (Gandhinagar) both show 'posted 3 days ago' on 21 Oct 2026, so about 18 Oct. The company jobs list shows only these two, both 3 days old, with no older or repeated Satyamev postings. The date is relative only, so say 'this week' and never an exact date. SIGNAL IS WEAK, GENERIC AND HIRING-ONLY: two entry-level roles with boilerplate duties prove staffing intent, not missed or late enquiries. The company's chosen fix for enquiry handling is more people (salesperson, specialist and possibly a telecaller), which is the thing we would replace or supplement. No pain was observed anywhere: no review complaints, no RERA complaint hits (my search found nothing about Satyamev or Royal 4), no complaints about slow replies. The pain remains a hypothesis. The LinkedIn titles also carry 'Mahesana' although the company has no Mehsana project on its site. The Gandhinagar job is posted under 'Prachi Patel', shown as a student. Poster labels and the template look sloppy, so I would not read much into the JD wording.

OWNER NOT VERIFIED, but the finder's label is not contradicted: the Real Estate Salesperson job names 'Yash Patel, Managing director' as poster. A web search surfaced a LinkedIn profile (linkedin.com/in/yash-patel-2a5945128) whose snippet says Managing Director of Shree Gayatri Satyamev Realty Pvt Ltd since Sept 2018, and also a civil engineer role at 'Satyamev Group' Aug 2023 to Feb 2024. A person cannot be MD from 2018 and an engineer in 2023, so the title is self-entered and soft. I could not open the profile (HTTP 999) and did not try to bypass it. MCA directors were not checked and web searches found no director record. The company site and company LinkedIn page name no principal. Only 'Vijay' appears, in emails, with no surname or title. So: do not name or title anyone in the message. Address it to the Satyamev Group sales team or write 'Hi team', or use only 'Vijay' if the email is sent to vijay@.

CONTACT ROUTE IS SAFE BUT THIN (checked on raw homepage HTML): tel: links for +91 98245 38519 and +91 98240 36846 (unlabelled), mailto for sales.satyamev@gmail.com, vijay@satyamevgroup.com and vijaypatel289@gmail.com. There is no wa.me link, no WhatsApp text and no chat widget. Social links are only Instagram and Facebook (facebook.com/satyamevbuilder/, unreadable by fetch). The emails are business-published, so email is the only clean route. Do not use the houssed.com WhatsApp number (81691 14718), which is a portal line and not theirs. A WhatsApp first touch to the unlabelled mobiles would be unsolicited, and the campaign data (cold WhatsApp templates 0/3) argues against it.

DIGITAL MATURITY IS LOW, a double-edged sign: satyamevgroup.com is a one-page WordPress site whose sitemap lists only the homepage (lastmod 2026-08-18). /contact-us/ and /about-us/ return 404. The homepage has no GA, Meta pixel, CRM or chat widget, and no enquiry form fields, only a brochure-PDF menu and a contact-form-7 plugin that has no visible form. The Instagram bio has no phone or WhatsApp. This means no strong existing automation or vendor, but it also means no sign they run click-to-WhatsApp ads or have a WhatsApp-first enquiry flow. Enquiries probably arrive by phone, portals (Houssed, PropertyPistol, 99acres) and walk-ins. The premise 'a buyer sends an enquiry on WhatsApp at night' is therefore unobserved, and their appetite for software is uncertain.

SIZE AND PAY SIGNALS ARE INFLATED OR CONFLICTING: LinkedIn says 51-200 employees but 'View all 8'. Weekday says 3. LinkedIn and the website claim 100+ projects and Australia, Dubai and Canada presence, but Houssed lists 18 projects, 2 ongoing, 16 completed (the website shows 3 ongoing plus 1 upcoming). Prices of about Rs 57 lakh and up per unit for Royal 4 (portal prices) and an active Instagram (posts shown 10, 13 and 17 Oct; the page dates are out of order) suggest they can pay for a modest tool. Do not state size, years or project counts in outreach. Satyamev Developers (Kalp Patel) and Satyamev Group look like separate or sister entities, so do not mix them.

FINDER'S OPENING LINE: the qualifier's replacement is acceptable because the hiring facts are supported, but change the closing question. The company publishes no WhatsApp number, so the better question is: 'When someone enquires about Royal 4 or Royal 5 by phone or WhatsApp after office hours, does anyone reply within a few minutes?' Even better is to avoid naming WhatsApp as an assumed channel and ask how after-hours and portal enquiries get a first response. Do not claim missed enquiries, ads, a CRM, or a telecaller team (the telecaller duties came from a search summary; the Weekday page I fetched has no JD and no date, and it is not a signal).

WHY NOT A STRONGER REFUTE: no stale signal, no wrong company (real developer with projects and a company-domain email), no agency or vendor, and no hostile positioning against bots or AI found. WHY NOT A CLEAN B: the key facts of owner, pain and WhatsApp use are all unconfirmed. If the bar is 'positively confirm owner, pain and channel' this lead fails. If the bar is 'real, recent, reachable, no contradicting evidence' it passes narrowly. Treat it as a low-intent hiring-angle test and compare any reply rate against explicit-ask leads.

judge.verdict_short: Bad result, said plainly: about 96 queries across 5 angles gave 1 candidate. That candidate is a weak hiring signal and the skeptic regraded it to C+. Zero builders or brokers were found asking for WhatsApp enquiry automation themselves. Caveat: this ran on Claude WebSearch/WebFetch with Apify blocked, not on Gemini Deep Research, so it does not prove the prompt fails in Gemini. It does show that explicit-ask leads are not publicly findable in useful numbers. The prompt as written is aimed at a target that mostly does not exist in public text.
judge.hit_rate_summary: Found -> owner verified -> survived skeptic, per angle (queries in brackets). Explicit English (17): 0 -> 0 -> 0. Explicit Hindi/Hinglish/Gujarati (22): 0 -> 0 -> 0. Hiring (13): 1 -> 0 verified (1 LIKELY, one soft LinkedIn label) -> 1 survived, but only as a weak low-intent test (C+). Ads/launch (18): 0 -> 0 -> 0. Complaints/founder voice (26): 0 -> 0 -> 0. Total: about 96 queries, 1 candidate, 0 verified owners, 0 explicit asks. The 1 survivor is Satyamev Group, Ahmedabad/Gandhinagar. It has two entry-level sales ads about 3 days old that mention lead follow-up. No pain was observed, WhatsApp use is unknown, and the website is thin. The owner label (Yash Patel, MD) is self-entered and not safe to use by name.
judge.best_angle: Hiring. It is the only angle that produced a dated, checkable signal. The method that worked: a logged-out LinkedIn public jobs search page with the past-2-weeks filter, then opening each job page for the relative date and poster. It found about 4 near misses (Vistara, VR Ahmedabad, TDS Properties, Sankalp) that were rejected only because no owner could be verified. Even so, hiring shows staffing intent, not missed enquiries, so treat it as Tier 2 context and not as 'someone who asked'.
judge.useless_angles: Explicit asks in English and in Hindi/Hinglish/Gujarati: zero first-person posts, because search returned only CRM, AI-calling and WhatsApp vendors (Makanify, BrokerDost, Codingclave, VSCRM, Rynow, DaeBuild and others). Complaints/founder voice: the only dated thread (Oculus Infra) was a year old and about construction defects, not unanswered enquiries. Ads/launch: untestable here, because the Meta Ad Library was unreachable and Apify was blocked. That is a tooling gap, not evidence the signal does not exist. The one new RERA project found (Auracle, Makarba, Ue Living LLP, 16 Sep 2026) has no website, owner or contact.
judge.intent_leads_exist_answer: Not in useful numbers, and not findable in public. Builders and brokers do not post 'I need WhatsApp automation' or 'my enquiries go unanswered' in indexable text. That talk sits in private WhatsApp groups and logged-in Facebook groups. This matches the 9 Oct source test, where explicit asks were rare. Gujarat builders are also pitched CRMs constantly by local vendors, so the cold bar is high. Only trigger-based signals (hiring, Meta ads with a WhatsApp button, new RERA registrations) can be found and dated. They show likely need, not a request, so expect low reply rates. Campaign 1 had 0 replies from 9 contacted, which is the benchmark to compare against. A Gemini run could add 0 to 2 explicit leads at best, and each would need re-checking.
blocked_sources: Apify, both connectors: 'Monthly usage hard limit exceeded', every run refused (US$0 spent). This blocked Meta Ad Library scraping and Google Maps reviews.
Meta Ad Library: JavaScript-rendered, WebFetch fails ('socket hang up').
reddit.com, magicbricks.com, economictimes and timesofindia: refused by the fetch/search tool.
DuckDuckGo: bot challenge, not bypassed. Google via WebFetch: no results. Bing: loads but returns unrelated results.
Facebook pages and posts, Instagram, YouTube search/comments: login wall or JS only, no post text or dates readable.
MouthShut: 403. LinkedIn post feeds: not scraped by rule. LinkedIn profiles: HTTP 999.
Official GujRERA portal: JS search UI, not usable via WebFetch. Third-party gujrera.com and aurumproptech.in worked only for single project pages.
Reached fine: logged-out LinkedIn public jobs pages (best source), Weekday and TeamLease snippets (undated), consumercomplaints.in.
prompt_v2_edits: Demote explicit asks (English, Hinglish, Gujarati) to a footnote section, 'return 0 if none'. Make hiring, Meta Ad Library WhatsApp-CTA ads and new RERA registrations the main angles.
Add a hard exclusion: ignore any page from a CRM, AI-calling, WhatsApp-automation or lead-gen vendor or agency. Include the known Gujarat vendor names so they stop filling results.

Require a verbatim quote, the post URL and a date shown on the page for every signal. Undated job-board listings (Weekday, TeamLease) count as context only. Accept LinkedIn 'N days ago' and ask the model to state the fetch date.
Say that 0 leads in any section is acceptable, and forbid padding. Add a 'sources I could not access' field. The model must list blocked sources instead of inferring from snippets.

Split the owner rule. VERIFIED needs 2 independent sources (LinkedIn plus MCA, GujRERA authorised person, or the company's own site). If only a poster label exists, mark UNVERIFIED and use a company-published contact with a 'Hi team' opener and no personal name or title. Today's rule rejected 4 real near misses and let a self-entered 'MD' label through.
Drop the RERA-number requirement or mark it optional. It cannot be met without the official portal. Add the GujRERA trick: the number ends in DDMMYY, which dates the approval.

Make it two-step. Step 1 is discovery of builders from LinkedIn jobs (past 2 weeks), Meta Ad Library and GujRERA. Step 2 enriches the owner and contact. Tier A needs a stacked signal, for example a hiring ad plus an active WhatsApp or Send-message ad.
Add a field pain_observed (yes/no) and a hypothesis label. A hiring ad alone is capped at Tier B or C.
Do not assume WhatsApp is the enquiry channel in opening lines. Ask how after-hours and portal enquiries get a first reply, and add must_not_claim for missed enquiries, ads and CRM.
Widen the hiring sweep to Surat, Rajkot, Vadodara, Gandhinagar, Anand, Bhavnagar and Mehsana, and add Naukri and Indeed company pages.
Positioning note: do not lead with 'CRM', because Gujarat builders already see local CRM pitches. Lead with the first WhatsApp reply and the site-visit slot.
judge.recommended_next_step: Stop spending effort on hunting explicit asks. In order: (1) Do a read-only, no-login Meta Ad Library check in the browser pane, by hand or with Apify once quota returns. Use the Squareyards builder names (Aadi Makers, Tirupati Construction, Kailash Corporation, Sahaj Buildcon, Raghuvir Buildcon, Hrishikesh Ventures, Bhumika Buildcon) plus Auracle (Ue Living LLP) and Satyamev, and look for active click-to-WhatsApp ads. This is the strongest untested signal. (2) Re-run the v2 prompt in Gemini Deep Research when its quota resets, as a real A/B against this Claude-tool run, and re-check every item it returns. (3) Enrich the 4 hiring near misses (Vistara, VR Ahmedabad, TDS Properties, Sankalp) with a website and owner check. (4) If you want a cheap live test, send one short email from your side to the company-published address for Satyamev ('Hi team', no personal name, no WhatsApp assumed, nothing on WhatsApp). This needs your approval. Log it as a low-intent hiring test and compare its reply rate with the 0/9 from campaign 1.
